Leonhard Euler is a mathematician. Euler has been called a "universal genius" who "was fully equipped with almost unlimited powers of imagination, intellectual gifts and extraordinary memory".
What is the atomic number of Molybdenum?
Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.
What is the atomic number of Iron?
Iron is a chemical element; it has symbol Fe (from Latin ferrum 'iron') and atomic number 26.
In what year was Edward Teller born?
Edward Teller: Born in Austria-Hungary in 1908, Teller emigrated to the US in the 1930s, one of the many so-called "Martians", a group of Hungarian scientist émigrés.
In what year was HIV discovered?
HIV: Without treatment, the average survival time after infection with HIV is estimated to be 9 to 11 years, depending on the HIV subtype.
In what year was Platinum discovered?
Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
Rituximab: Pfizer. It is given by slow intravenous infusion.
Which country is Grumman F-14 Tomcat from?

Grumman F-14 Tomcat: United States. The Grumman F-14 Tomcat is an American carrier-capable supersonic, twin-engine, tandem two-seat, twin-tail, all-weather-capable variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Thorium?
Thorium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.
Who is credited with discovering Cauchy–Schwarz inequality?
Cauchy–Schwarz inequality: Viktor Bunyakovsky. It is considered one of the most important and widely used inequalities in mathematics.
Who is credited with discovering Phosphorus?
Phosphorus: Hennig Brand. Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.

This alternative-medicine practice, a component of traditional Chinese medicine, involves inserting thin needles into the body, though its underlying theories are considered pseudoscientific by mainstream science — what's the practice called?
Acupuncture is a form of alternative medicine and a component of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in which thin needles are inserted into the body.
Ranging from South Florida to Peru, this reptile is the most widespread member of its family in the Americas and one of only two species that commonly thrive in saltwater — which species?
American crocodile (Crocodylus acutus) is a species of crocodilian found in the Neotropics.
With 1,248 built, this turboprop's design was adapted from an earlier Soviet transport aircraft and became NATO's 'Cub' — which four-engine workhorse?
Antonov An-12 (NATO reporting name: Cub) is a four-engined turboprop transport aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
Which genus of early hominins, which lived in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, gave rise to the genera Homo, Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus?
Australopithecus (-loh-; or, os-, from Latin australis southern 'grc' and (pthkos) ape) is a genus of early hominins that existed in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene.
This red-orange compound, formed from the breakdown of heme, is further processed into pigments that give feces their brown color and urine its straw-yellow hue. What is it?
Bilirubin (BR) (adopted from German, originally bili, for bile, plus ruber, Latin for red) is a red-orange compound that occurs as the reduction product of biliverdin, a breakdown product of heme.
This flowering plant family is known for flowers with four petals arranged in a cross shape, and includes crops ranging from leafy greens to root vegetables to condiment seeds. Name the family?
Brassicaceae (the older but equally valid) Cruciferae is a medium-sized and economically important family of flowering plants commonly known as the mustards, the crucifers, or the cabbage family.

Spread through contact with infected feces and capable of killing up to 91% of untreated cases, this highly contagious virus mainly strikes dogs and wolves but can also infect foxes, cats, and skunks — what's the virus?
Canine parvovirus (also referred to as CPV, CPV2, or parvo) is a contagious virus mainly affecting dogs and wolves.
This English polymath is credited with inventing the first mechanical computer and designing an unrealized 'analytical engine' programmed using ideas borrowed from the Jacquard loom. Who is he?
Charles Babbage (26 December 1791 - 18 October 1871) was an English polymath.
Born near Toulouse, this French inventor is remembered chiefly as an aviation pioneer — though in 1870 he was also an early enthusiast of cycling in France; who was he?
Clément Ader (French; 2 April 1841 - 3 May 1925) was a French inventor and engineer who was born near Toulouse in Muret, Haute-Garonne, and died in Toulouse.
Derived from Greek words meaning universe and study of, this scientific and philosophical field examines the nature of existence at the grandest scale — what is it called?
Cosmology (from Ancient Greek (cosmos) 'the universe, the world' and - (logia) 'study of') is the study of the nature of the universe, the cosmos.
The word names both a noun — a plan or proposal made by a thinking agent — and a verb for developing one, always aiming to satisfy goals while weighing function and aesthetics; what is it?
Design is the concept or proposal for an object, process, or system.
Most of the 68 species sharing this name live in Eurasia and Africa, with only two found in North America — and "true" ones are merely a subfamily; what bird is it?
Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.
This Ancient Greek polymath, who became chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, is considered the founder of geography as a discipline and coined much of its early terminology — who is he?

First recognised in the 1950s but not formally defined until 1990, this disorder of widespread chronic pain — often with fatigue and memory trouble — has no known cause and is treated multidisciplinarily. What is it?
Fibromyalgia (FM) is a long-term condition characterised by widespread chronic pain.

This computer scientist demonstrated a working prototype of his operating system CP/M in 1974 and later founded Digital Research — his invention of the BIOS helped make the personal computer revolution possible. Who is he?
Gary Kildall (May 19, 1942 - July 11, 1994) was an American computer scientist and microcomputer entrepreneur.
Defined as one joule of absorbed radiation energy per kilogram of matter, this SI measure is used in radiotherapy dosing and predicting acute radiation sickness — which measure is this?
Gray (unit) (symbol: Gy) is the unit of ionizing radiation dose in the International System of Units (SI), defined as the absorption of one joule of radiation energy per kilogram of matter.
Classified as acute if it resolves within six months and chronic if it persists longer, this inflammation of the liver can progress to cirrhosis or liver cancer — which condition?
Hepatitis is inflammation of the liver tissue. Acute hepatitis can resolve on its own, progress to chronic hepatitis, or (rarely) result in acute liver failure.

This altered mental state involves intensely focused attention, reduced awareness of surroundings, and heightened responsiveness to suggestion, though scientists still debate whether it's truly a distinct state of consciousness — what is it?

Hypnosis is a human condition involving focused attention (the selective attention/selective inattention hypothesis, SASI), reduced peripheral awareness, and an enhanced capacity to respond to suggestion.
Eaten raw or turned into jams and wine, this round Brazilian fruit is famous for growing directly on the trunk of its own tree — what is it?
Jabuticaba is a round, edible fruit produced by a jaboticaba tree (Plinia cauliflora), also known as Brazilian grapetree.

An Alberta-raised classical liberal who earned his PhD in clinical psychology at McGill and taught at Harvard before the University of Toronto, this commentator drew huge attention in the late 2010s — who is he?
Jordan Peterson (born 12 June 1962) is a Canadian psychologist, author, and media commentator.

Sold under a well-known brand name, this medication treats several types of epilepsy including focal and tonic-clonic seizures, and also helps stabilize mood by reducing future depressive episodes in bipolar disorder — which drug?
Lamotrigine (luh-), sold under the brand name Lamictal among others, is a medication used to treat epilepsy and stabilize mood in bipolar disorder.
Named from the Greek word for 'stone,' this alkali metal with symbol Li tarnishes from silver to black in air and was once mined mainly from pegmatite minerals — what is it?
Lithium (from Ancient) is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

Native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere, this genus of 32 to 57 deciduous trees and shrubs in the rose family includes the ancestors of a familiar orchard fruit plus ornamental wild and crab varieties — what's the genus?
Malus (or) is a genus of about 32-57 species of small deciduous trees or shrubs in the family Rosaceae, including the domesticated orchard apple, crab apples, and wild apples.
Together with the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, this monoplane fighter formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe's fighter force throughout the Second World War. What aircraft is it?
Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).
Its English name passed from Greek to Latin to Portuguese before landing in English in the early 1600s — which family of roughly 200 marine fish species boasts 16 genera?
Moray eel are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.
Composed of a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule, this microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney numbers between 1 and 1.5 million per healthy adult kidney — name it?

Nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney. The renal corpuscle consists of a tuft of capillaries called a glomerulus and a cup-shaped structure called Bowman's capsule.
Concerned with the most fundamental concept of all — being — this branch of metaphysics distinguishes non-repeatable particulars from repeatable universals like 'green' — what is the field?
Ontology is the philosophical study of being.
Named for the extra copy of chromosome 13 found in affected cells, this condition — related to Down and Edwards syndromes — disrupts normal organ development — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome is a syndrome caused by a chromosomal abnormality, in which some or all of the cells of the body contain extra genetic material from chromosome 13.
This anxiety disorder involves an irrational, excessive, and persistent fear of a specific object or situation, often leading sufferers to go to great lengths to avoid it — what is it called?
Phobia is an anxiety disorder, defined by an irrational, unrealistic, persistent and excessive fear of an object or situation.
Named from the Greek for an infinite carbon chain it would ultimately become, this class of organic compounds strings together alternating single and triple bonds. What is it called?
Polyyne is any organic compound with alternating single and triple bonds; that is, a series of consecutive alkynes, (CC)n with n greater than 1.
Which industry has expanded from traditional books and newspapers to e-books, websites, and video games, with giants like Thomson Reuters and News Corp among its biggest players?
Publishing is the process of making information, literature, music, software, and other content, whether in physical or digital form, available to the public for sale or free of charge.
This positive-sense RNA virus in the Enterovirus genus is the most common viral infectious agent in humans and the leading cause of the common cold — name the virus?
Rhinovirus (from the Ancient) is a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA virus belonging to the genus Enterovirus in the family Picornaviridae.
This Harvard political scientist argued in a 1993 theory that future conflict would erupt not between countries but between cultures — a 'clash of civilizations.' Who was he?
Samuel P. Huntington (April 18, 1927 - December 24, 2008) was an American political scientist, adviser, and academic.
Believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso, this toy dog breed originated in Tibet — name the breed?
Shih Tzu is a toy dog or pet dog breed originating from Tibet and believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso.

Meaning 'pore bearer' in Greek, this phylum of sessile, filter-feeding marine invertebrates has tube-like bodies of jelly-like material sandwiched between thin cell layers, letting water circulate through countless pores — name the animal group?
Sponge are primarily marine invertebrates of the animal phylum Porifera (meaning 'pore bearer').

In the nervous system, this structure lets one neuron send or receive signals with a neighboring cell, and comes in both chemical and electrical varieties — the electrical kind linked directly through gap junctions — name this structure?
Synapse is a structure that allows a neuron to exchange (receive or send) signals with another cell in its immediate vicinity.

This weakly radioactive silvery metal, atomic number 90, tarnishes olive-grey in air, and its most stable isotope has a half-life of about 14 billion years — roughly the age of the universe. What element is this?
Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.

It spawned a maritime patrol version (the Tu-142) and even a passenger airliner (the Tu-114), and Russia expects to keep flying this propeller-driven bomber until at least 2040 — which aircraft is it?
Tupolev Tu-95 (NATO reporting name: "Bear") is a Soviet nuclear-capable large, four-engine turboprop strategic bomber and missile platform.
Leading organic chemistry at DuPont's Experimental Station, this troubled chemist not only invented nylon but also helped lay the groundwork for neoprene. Who was he?
Wallace Carothers (April 27, 1896 - April 29, 1937) was an American chemist, inventor, and the leader of organic chemistry at DuPont, who was credited with the invention of nylon.
Also known as AZT, this was the very first antiretroviral drug used against HIV/AIDS, and can be given during birth to prevent mother-to-child spread — what is it?
Zidovudine (ZDV), also known as azidothymidine (AZT), was the first antiretroviral medication used to prevent and treat HIV/AIDS.
Nicknamed the cell's "molecular unit of currency," this energy-carrying molecule powers muscle contraction and nerve impulses, dropping to ADP or AMP when spent — what is it?
Adenosine triphosphate: Energy-carrying molecule in living cells.
This French surgeon won a 1912 Nobel for pioneering blood-vessel suturing and later teamed with aviator Charles Lindbergh to build an early perfusion pump for organ work. Who was he?
Alexis Carrel: French surgeon and biologist (1873–1944)
Domesticated in Southwest China roughly 2,000 years ago, this corm-producing plant is nicknamed 'devil's tongue' and gets boiled down into a jelly-like noodle called shirataki — what is it?
Amorphophallus konjac: Edible plant from Yunnan, China.
This self-taught Dutch draper turned lensmaker began exploring microbial life with his own single-lensed microscopes in the 1670s, earning him the title 'Father of Microbiology' — who was he?
Writing in 499 CE that he was 23 years old, this pioneering Indian scholar's explicit discussion of the relativity of motion marks him as an early physicist too — who was he?
Native to the steppes of Central Asia, this two-humped pack animal's cold and drought tolerance made it indispensable to Silk Road caravans — what is it?
Bactrian camel: Species of mammal of Asia.
Native to Southeast Asia, the heart-shaped leaves of this pepper-family vine are chewed with areca nut, despite links to serious health risks — which plant?
Betel: Species of plant. Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.

Commonly called the Triple Seven, this American wide-body airliner is the world's largest twinjet and the most-built wide-body airplane. It was designed to bridge the gap between the twin-engined 767 and quad-engined 747. What is it?
This Asian insect species, first found in Pennsylvania in 1998, cost Mid-Atlantic apple growers $37 million in a single year and now threatens hazelnut harvests worldwide — what is it?

Brown marmorated stink bug: Species of Pentatomid insect. The brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.
White, green, oolong, and black tea all come from the same evergreen shrub, simply processed to different levels of oxidation — name the plant species?
Camellia sinensis: Species of evergreen shrub. Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
Native to the rainforests of New Guinea and northeastern Australia, this flightless ratite is the fourth-tallest and third-heaviest living bird, trailing only the ostriches and the emu?
Sometimes dubbed the 'central science' for sitting between physics and biology, this field studies how matter is composed, behaves, and transforms in reactions — what is it?
Chemistry: Scientific study of matter's behavior and properties.
This inherited birth defect from a RUNX2 gene mutation leaves the collarbones underdeveloped or missing, letting the shoulders touch in front of the chest — which condition?
Cleidocranial dysostosis: Birth defect of the collarbones, skull, and teeth.
Best known for its powerful, beautiful song, this small Old World flycatcher sometimes hybridizes with a closely related thrush species where their ranges overlap — which bird?
Common nightingale: Species of bird. Its range partly overlaps with that of the more northerly thrush nightingale (Luscinia luscinia), a closely related species with which hybrids have occurred.
These feather-gilled freshwater crustaceans share their taxonomic order with lobsters and turn up in everything from brooks to rice paddies — what are they?
Crayfish: Freshwater crustaceans. Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.
The first Western European combat aircraft to break Mach 2 in level flight, achieving the feat in October 1958, which French fighter jet family was this?
Dassault Mirage III: French supersonic fighter/interceptor aircraft.

Discovered in Arizona in the 1940s and first classified as a species of Megalosaurus, this theropod was reassigned to a new genus in 1970 once paleontologists noticed the twin crests on its skull — which dinosaur?
Dilophosaurus: Genus of theropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic.

Coined by Robert Spitzer in the late 1970s to replace the notion of a "depressive personality," this condition resembles major depression but lingers for at least two years — and now goes by "persistent depressive disorder." What was its original name?
Dysthymia: Psychiatric disorder defined by chronic depression.
Caused by viruses like herpes simplex or rabies, this inflammation of the brain can bring fever, confusion, and a stiff neck — what is this condition?

Encephalitis: Inflammation of the brain. The severity can be variable with symptoms including reduction or alteration in consciousness, aphasia, headache, fever, confusion, a stiff neck, and vomiting.
This complex-analysis identity states that e raised to the power of ix equals cosine x plus i times sine x, linking exponential and trigonometric functions — what is it called?
Euler's formula: Complex exponential in terms of sine and cosine. The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and is also called Euler's formula in this more general case.
Carnivora splits into two suborders, dog-like and cat-like — which one groups cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids together?
This infection and inflammation of hair follicles produces pimples with white tips anywhere on hair-covered skin — what is the condition called?
Folliculitis: Human and animal disease of follicles.
Once classified under two different bacterial genera, this nonmotile coccobacillus forms small gray colonies on chocolate agar and has its own colistin-oxolinic acid selective medium — which species?
Gardnerella vaginalis: Species of bacterium. Gardnerella vaginalis is a species of Gram-variable-staining facultative anaerobic bacteria.
Nicknamed creeping charlie and alehoof, this aromatic mint-family creeper is eaten as a salad green in some countries but reviled as an invasive lawn weed in North America — what plant is it?
Glechoma hederacea: Species of plant in the mint family. It is commonly known as ground-ivy, gill-over-the-ground, creeping charlie, alehoof, tunhoof, catsfoot, field balm, and run-away-robin.
Marketed under the brand name Mucinex, this expectorant medication has been used to loosen chest congestion since at least 1933 — what is it?
Guaifenesin: Expectorant medication. It may be used in combination with other medications.

First proposed as early as the 3rd century BC by Aristarchus of Samos, this astronomical model places the sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe. What is this superseded model called?
Heliocentrism: Sun-centered astronomical model. Historically, heliocentrism was opposed to geocentrism, which placed Earth at the center.
Nicknamed 'Hobbit,' this extinct species of small archaic humans stood about 1.1 meters tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago — which species?
Homo floresiensis: Extinct small human species found in Flores.

Typically begun with an induction of preliminary instructions, this state of focused attention and heightened suggestibility is debated as either an altered trance or a form of imaginative role-play — what is it?
Hypnosis: State of increased suggestibility. There are competing theories explaining hypnosis and related phenomena.

This analytical framework describes how overlapping identities like race, gender, and class combine to create unique experiences of discrimination or privilege, and emerged partly as a critique of mainstream feminism — which concept?
Intersectionality: Theory of discrimination. The term intersectionality was coined by Kimberlé Crenshaw in 1989.
A French soldier turned naturalist, this early proponent of biological evolution published the three-volume 'Flore françoise' and joined the French Academy of Sciences in 1779 — who is he?
Nicknamed 'Iron Annie,' which corrugated-skin transport plane began life as a 1930 civilian airliner before Nazi Germany converted it for military use?
Biosynthesized in the body from the amino acid tyrosine, this compound is the direct precursor to dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine — what is it?
L-DOPA: Chemical compound. As is true for many molecules, the human body produces only one of these isomers (the l-DOPA form).
Sold under the brand name Xyzal, this less-sedating second-generation antihistamine for hay fever and hives was patented in 1965 but not approved in the US until 2007 — what is it?
Levocetirizine: Antihistamine medication. It is classified as a second-generation antihistamine and works by blocking histamine H1-receptors.
Nicknamed the sea devil, frogfish, or fishing frog, this species anchors a major commercial fishery in the Irish Sea and ranges from the Barents Sea to the Mediterranean — which fish?
Lophius piscatorius: Species of fish. Lophius piscatorius, commonly known as the angler, toadfish, sea frog, fishing frog, frogfish, or sea devil, is a species of Lophius in the family Lophiidae.
This category of health conditions arises from too few, too many, or an imbalance of nutrients, and can cause anything from stunted growth to obesity. What is it called?
Malnutrition: Medical condition caused by receiving too little or too many nutrients.

Entering US Navy service in 1961 before the Marines and Air Force adopted it too, this twin-engine supersonic jet became America's most-produced supersonic military aircraft with 5,195 built — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II: Fighter aircraft family developed from 1958.
Sold as Flagyl, this antibiotic and antiprotozoal fights everything from giardiasis to trichomoniasis — but it's notorious for leaving a metallic taste in your mouth — what is it?
Metronidazole: Antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication. Metronidazole, sold under the brand name Flagyl and Metrogyl among others, is an antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication.
Making up about 23% of all named marine organisms, this phylum is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after the arthropods — what is it?
In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature into healthy ones, and some cases progress into acute myeloid leukemia — what is it called?
Myelodysplastic syndrome: Diverse collection of blood-related cancers.
Unlike its niacin cousin, this form of vitamin B3 treats pellagra without causing skin flushing, and as a cream is used to fade acne scars and reduce hyperpigmentation — what is it?

With atomic number 118, this synthetic element boasts the highest atomic number and mass of any known element, and was named to honor the physicist who led the hunt for the periodic table's heaviest members — what is it?
Oganesson: Chemical element with atomic number 118 (Og)

Powered by NADH and FADH₂ handed off from glycolysis and the citric acid cycle, this mitochondrial pathway is how nearly all aerobic organisms produce ATP — far more efficiently than fermentation. What's it called?
Oxidative phosphorylation: Metabolic pathway. Oxidative phosphorylation uses these molecules and O2 to produce ATP, which is used throughout the cell whenever energy is needed.
Named Pisum sativum by Carl Linnaeus in 1753, this pulse crop's pods are botanically a fruit containing seeds with green or yellow cotyledons — what vegetable is it?
Pea: Species of plant with edible seeds.
Its name combines the Greek words for 'love' and 'tree,' and with over 600 accepted species it's the second-largest genus in the arum family after Anthurium — which popular houseplant genus?
Known informally for resembling a certain dairy product due to its shape, this popular edible fungus grows wild across temperate and subtropical forests worldwide — what is its scientific name?
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This colorless, odorless nerve agent can kill within minutes of inhalation and was banned by the 1993 Chemical Weapons Convention — what is it?
Sarin: Chemical compound and chemical warfare nerve agent.
Drawing on fields from anthropology to epidemiology, this scientific discipline studies everything from sexual development in puberty to gender identity and paraphilias — which field of study?
Sexology: Scientific study of human sexuality.

Once extracted from the ashes of certain salt-absorbing plants and now produced from ordinary salt and limestone via the Solvay process, this alkaline compound is also known as washing soda or soda ash — what is it?
Sodium carbonate: Chemical compound. Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.
Known for a synchronized aerial swarming display called murmuration, this glossy-plumed bird family includes talkative mynas as members — which birds?
Starling: Family of birds. The Sturnidae are named for the genus Sturnus, which in turn comes from the Latin word for starling, sturnus.
This South African biologist made a tiny roundworm, C. elegans, the model organism for studying how bodies develop, sharing a 2002 Nobel for the work — who is he?
Sydney Brenner: South African biologist and Nobel prize winner (1927–2019)
Developed under the codename 'WhiteStar' and unveiled in Hawthorne, California in 2009, this full-size electric sedan won Motor Trend's Car of the Year in 2013 — which car?
Tesla Model S: Battery-electric full-size car. The Tesla Model S is a battery-electric, four-door full-size car that was produced by the American automaker Tesla from 2012 to 2026.
Commonly called jock itch, this contagious fungal infection of the groin and buttocks causes an intensely itchy, red, scaly rash with a well-defined curved border — what is it?
Tinea cruris: Fungal infection. It is often associated with athlete's foot and fungal nail infections, excessive sweating, and sharing of infected towels or sports clothing.
Nicknamed 'rabbit fever' and spread by ticks, deer flies or contact with infected animals, this bacterial infection causes fever, skin ulcers and swollen lymph nodes — what is it?
Tularemia: Infectious disease caused by the bacterium Francisella tularensis.
Heading the office that ran nearly all of America's WWII military R&D, this engineer launched the early Manhattan Project and later drove the creation of the National Science Foundation. Who was he?
Awarded the 1932 Nobel Prize 'for the creation of quantum mechanics,' this German physicist also led his country's wartime nuclear program — who was he?
This citrus fruit of Chinese origin is believed to be a natural hybrid of a wild mandarin subspecies and the ichang papeda — what fruit?
Yuzu: Citrus fruit and plant. Yuzu (Citrus × junos, from Japanese 柚子 or ユズ;) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.
The symbol for promethium is Pm. Promethium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pm and atomic number 61.
Sodium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for sodium is Na. Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na and atomic number 11.

Who among these is a comedian?
Gad Elmaleh is a comedian. Gad Elmaleh (Arabic: جاد المالح, Gād el-Māleḥ, Berber languages: ⴳⴰⴷ ⵍⵎⴰⵍⵃ; born 19 April 1971) is a Moroccan-Canadian stand-up comedian and actor.
In what year was Christopher Lloyd born?
Christopher Lloyd: Christopher Allen Lloyd (born October 22, 1938) is an American actor.
In what year was Angela White born?
Angela White: Angela Gabrielle White (born 1984 or 1985) is an Australian pornographic film actress and director.
In what year was Christopher Lee born?
Christopher Lee: Sir Christopher Frank Carandini Lee (27 May 1922 – 7 June 2015) was an English actor and singer.
In what year was Stanley Kubrick born?
Stanley Kubrick (July 26, 1928 – March 7, 1999) was an American filmmaker and photographer.
In what year was Michelle Monaghan born?
